headline.purpose: Page titles. The largest type anywhere in the product; nothing sits above it.

body.purpose: The workhorse: table cells, form values, descriptions, nav items. Prose caps at 65-75ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase column headers, stat labels, metadata keys. Always Quiet Ink.

data.purpose: Every numeric value that sits in a column. Monospace with tabular figures, always.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, sheets, dropdowns, popovers. The only shadow that appears at rest, and only on things that genuinely float above the page.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Interactive panels on :hover and :focus-visible only. Never at rest. Pairs with a border shift to Action Blue and a 1px translate.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Default for color, border, and background transitions on controls and rows.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Interactive panel hover: shadow, border, and transform together.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions. No bounce, no elastic anywhere in the system.

narrative.overview:
A press box desk with the league's record book open on it. Everything on that desk earns its place by being consulted: the standings, the box score, the schedule, the archive of past seasons. Nothing is there to set a mood. The record book is authoritative because it is complete and because it is the same every time you open it — and the desk is fast because whoever works at it is looking things up while play continues.

That fusion is the whole system. From the record book: squared corners, ruled lines, tabular figures, an archive that never loses a season. From the press box: density, speed, no ceremony between a question and its answer. The visual language is a broadcast stats graphic rendered for reading rather than for air — dense, ruled, unmistakably legible, and confident enough to present a Roblox volleyball league with the gravity of a real one.

What this system rejects is decoration standing in for authority. It does not use gradients to make a heading feel important, or shadows to make a card feel modern, or neon to make a competition feel exciting. Weight, rule lines, and tabular alignment carry all of it. If a surface needs an effect to read as serious, the surface is wrong.
keyCharacteristics: Square corners on every data surface — .panel resolves to a literal 0px radius
Flat by default; borders and tonal fills carry all in-page depth
One type family (Geist) for everything except numbers, which are always monospaced
Two accents with fixed jobs: blue acts, yellow locates
Dense by design — 12px vertical cell padding, 0.875rem body, 0.75rem labels
Desktop-first; density expands upward rather than collapsing downward

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Blue means act. Yellow means you are here. A screen that uses either color for any third purpose has broken the system, and the failure is invisible until a user misreads a highlighted row as a button.

rules.name: The No-Third-Accent Rule
rules.body: Anything that is not an action, a location, or a destructive operation is drawn from the neutral ramp. New categorical colors are prohibited. If a data category needs distinguishing, use position, weight, or rule lines before reaching for hue.

rules.name: The Inherited-Default Rule
rules.body: The current palette is Tailwind's stock zinc ramp with blue-500, yellow-400, and red-500 accents. That is a stated fact, not an endorsement. Any deliberate move away from it must change all of the accents together — a single re-tinted primary against stock zinc neutrals reads as a half-finished theme, which is worse than the default.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Geist carries headings, buttons, labels, body, and navigation. The monospace stack is the only second face, and it appears only on numbers. Introducing a display face is prohibited; it is the fastest available route to the esports look this brand rejects.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number that appears in a column gets font-mono tabular-nums. Non-negotiable. Proportional digits in a stat table cause the column to shimmer as values change and destroy the scannability that justifies the density in the first place.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: No clamp(), no viewport-relative type, anywhere. Users read this at a consistent desktop DPI, and a heading that shrinks inside a three-column shell looks broken rather than responsive.

rules.name: The Small-Type Floor
rules.body: 0.75rem is the floor for any text a user must read, and text at that size must sit in Ink or Quiet Ink on Surface — never Quiet Ink at reduced opacity. Below 12px, stat tables stop being dense and start being unreadable, which is the difference between this system and the spreadsheet it replaces.

rules.name: The Flat-Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the page flow casts a shadow at rest. If a surface needs to feel separated from what is behind it, change its tone or give it a border. A resting shadow-sm on a panel is the single clearest tell of an untouched component library.

rules.name: The Affordance-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Clickability is announced structurally at rest — border weight and a chevron — and confirmed with motion and shadow on hover. Discovery must never depend on the user hovering first.

rules.name: The Square-Corner Rule
rules.body: Data containers have zero radius. Controls get 2px. Badges get a pill. There is no fourth radius, and rounded-xl — shadcn's Card default — is prohibited on any new surface.

rules.name: The One Container Rule
rules.body: .panel is the only container vocabulary. shadcn's Card currently survives in seven files with rounded-xl and shadow-sm; those are deviations to migrate, not a second sanctioned system.

dos: Do use .panel for every container: square corners, 1px Rule border, Surface background, no resting shadow.
Do give clickable panels a full-strength border and a trailing chevron at rest, then add shadow-sm, an Action Blue border, and a 1px lift on hover.
Do set font-mono tabular-nums on every number that sits in a column.
Do keep Action Blue for what acts and Location Yellow for where you are. One job each.
Do build depth from the Page to Surface to Recessed tonal step and 1px Rule borders.
Do use fixed rem type sizes and let responsive behavior be structural — collapse the sidebar, stack the columns, make the table scroll.
Do hold body text to Ink and metadata to Quiet Ink. 0.75rem is the floor for anything a user must actually read.
Do keep transitions at 150-250ms on color, box-shadow, opacity, and transform — and pair every one with a prefers-reduced-motion alternative.
Do ship skeletons matching the real layout for loading, and empty states that name what will appear here and how it gets there.
donts: Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. app/(public)/home/HomePage.tsx:196 currently does this on the Season Standings heading. Gradient text is decorative, never meaningful — use weight and size.

Don't use border-left or border-right above 1px as a colored accent stripe. app/(public)/home/HomePage.tsx:186 currently does this on the empty state. Use a full border, a background tint, or nothing.

Don't ship the generic SaaS admin template: untouched shadcn defaults, rounded-2xl containers, purple gradient cards, hero-metric tiles. rounded-xl on a container is this look arriving one class at a time.
Don't ship the hobby-project dashboard: mismatched spacing, half-styled surfaces, default components dropped in unmodified. This is the failure mode CVRN exists to disprove.

Don't reach for esports and gaming tropes — neon accents, angular clip-path panels, RGB glows, aggressive italics, condensed display faces on scores. The obvious reflex for a gaming league and the wrong one for this brand.
Don't produce a spreadsheet on the web: an undifferentiated grid of numbers with no rank, no state, and no visual weight. Density is the point; density without hierarchy is the anti-reference.
Don't put a resting shadow on anything in the page flow. If it does not float above the page, it does not cast a shadow.
Don't introduce a second type family, a display face, or clamp()-sized headings.
Don't introduce a third accent hue for categorical data. Use position, weight, and rule lines.
Don't mix focus vocabularies. Controls use a 3px ring at 50% opacity; navigation currently uses 2px at full opacity. Converge on the 3px treatment.
Don't let a color be the only carrier of meaning. Win/loss, qualified/eliminated, and synced/failed each need a second cue — a glyph, a label, or position.
